facts.text: Ten Mile Creek is one of the healthiest waterways in the Chesapeake Bay watershed, supporting diverse aquatic life.
Scientists use Ten Mile Creek as a reference stream to gauge the health of other nearby streams.
It is the cleanest tributary feeding Little Seneca Reservoir, the emergency drinking water supply for 4.3 million DC residents.
In 1994, the county declared part of the Ten Mile Creek area a special protection area to preserve its water quality.
Ten Mile Creek begins near Thompsons Corner, about two miles northwest of Clarksburg, and flows south for 2.5 miles into Little Seneca Lake.
Friends of Ten Mile Creek and Little Seneca Reservoir, formed in 2014, protect the watershed from development that could harm its water quality.
